name: com.unity.netcode
description: Unity's Data Oriented Technology Stack (DOTS) multiplayer netcode layer - a high level netcode system built on entities. This package provides a foundation for creating networked multiplayer applications within DOTS.

_upm.changelog:
### Added
* Prediction tracing tool: this tool allows you to debug your prediction loop, diffing the client and server state per predicted tick and system for an in editor binary world setup.

### Changed
* Updated Single World Host smoothing to disabled by default for ghost prefabs.
* The methods in `DefaultDriverConstructor` don't need their `INetworkInterface` arguments to be unmanaged types anymore. This is in line with the same relaxation having been made in the Unity Transport package.
* The snapshot synchronisation system optionally no longer considers an unknown ghost type received on clients as an immediate fatal error. There is now a configurable timeout value `NetcodeConfig.GhostPrefabLoadingTimeout` which controls when this should be considered a fatal error. It also allows the client to destroy a ghost type (like unload a subscene with ghost prefab references) ahead of the server.
* `SnapshotHistorySize` is now configurable on a per-ghost-type basis, allowing you to reduce the memory consumed by a ghost's snapshot history for ghosts sent below the default 60Hz. The recommended value (and its tooltip) is visible in the ghost authoring UI.

### Fixed
* The `GhostAuthoringInspectionComponentEditor` no longer throws exceptions when it is open while exiting playmode.
* `NetworkStreamDriver.Disconnect` always disconnected on the first driver of the `NetworkDriverStore` instead of the driver the connection was established on. With more than one driver registered, this left the requested connection connected and could close an unrelated one instead.
* Removed an infinite retry loop in `GhostSendSystem`'s snapshot send loop: a `BeginSend` failure other than `NetworkPacketOverflow` (most commonly `NetworkSendQueueFull`) was never treated as fatal, so the job spun forever and hung the server instead of aborting.
* Prespawned ghosts that became irrelevant occasionally failed to become relevant again for a connection. A despawn still held for the interpolation delay could resolve onto the re-spawned entity and destroy it.
* `GhostDespawnSystem` now accounts for the fractional part of `NetworkTime.InterpolationTick`, so interpolated ghosts no longer despawn up to one tick ahead of the timeline the rest of the interpolation pipeline uses.
